extracted.intended_audience: experienced scientists, engineers, military officers, government civilians, and senior technical leaders considering DARPA Program Manager roles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for applying to and serving as a DARPA Program Manager (PM): role expectations, required qualifications, application materials, security and location requirements, and core responsibilities for overseeing high-risk/high-reward R&D programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Manager role expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Program Manager (PM) role defines DARPA. This organization is built around supporting their pioneering work. Freed from constraints, these innovators sail past convention and head into uncharted territory as they seek to change the trajectory of technology.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PMs conceive and develop seemingly impossible ideas to benefit national security; they are granted unparalleled freedom. The page emphasizes pioneering, unconstrained idea-generation and the expectation to change technology trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated exceptional accomplishment and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: “Typically, our ideal candidates have been brilliant, done incredible work, and produced game-changing ideas.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show a track record of high-impact achievements and novel contributions; there is no single profile, but demonstrable brilliance and past transformative work are primary signals of fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bold thinking, risk tolerance, and resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be “bold thinkers with the resilience to forge fearlessly into spaces unknown” and “move confidently forward with risks that cause most people to stop.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA seeks people comfortable with high uncertainty where failure is probable and where success can be revolutionary. Applicants should demonstrate willingness to take technical and programmatic risks and to persist through likely failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of urgency and goal-orientation within fixed tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must “operate with urgency and an inherent desire to leave a lasting mark during your fixed tenure.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PM appointment is time-limited (see term length); applicants should show an ability to set aggressive objectives and to deliver measurable progress quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and security eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: “As an agency within the U.S. Department of War, we require U.S. citizenship and the ability to secure and maintain an active security clearance.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. citizenship and the capacity to obtain and retain an active security clearance are mandatory prerequisites. Applicants who cannot satisfy these are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: “This position is based at our headquarters in Arlington, Virginia.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must be willing and able to work at DARPA headquarters in Arlington, VA (relocation support may be provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials required
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for a PM role, candidates should prepare the following: Cover letter; Resume; Preliminary proposal for a new program concept that does not contain any classified information and follows The Heilmeier Catechism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications lacking any of these components may not be considered. The preliminary proposal is a substantive piece used to assess idea quality; it must be unclassified and adhere to the Heilmeier framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary proposal constraints and standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary proposal must not contain classified information and must follow The Heilmeier Catechism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the page does not reproduce the Heilmeier questions, applicants are explicitly required to structure proposals according to that catechism (clear problem statement, metrics for success, approach, risks, resources, etc.). Keep the proposal unclassified and concise enough for initial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program management and technical oversight capability
rubrics_metrics.description: “DARPA PMs oversee portfolios of ambitious and rigorous research and development (R&D) programs, guiding collaborations between world-class researchers and engineers from academia, government, and industry.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate experience conceiving, structuring, and managing R&D programs, including coordinating multidisciplinary teams across sectors and shepherding projects from concept toward measurable technical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to build stakeholder engagement and feedback loops
rubrics_metrics.description: PMs proactively build stakeholder engagement from the military services and “construct valuable feedback loops between the agency and the warfighters we serve.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful PMs must engage end-users (e.g., military services), translate operational needs, and maintain two-way feedback to align technical efforts with real-world requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting and managing against aggressive program goals and technical milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: PMs “establish and manage against aggressive program goals, including detailed technical milestones to measure progress.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show experience defining clear, aggressive objectives and measurable technical milestones, and managing programs to those metrics; emphasis on rigor in progress measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term length and expectation of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: “If chosen, you will receive an appointment for a two-year term, with the possibility of an extension to four years. Every day that passes ... means one less day to make your mark.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The short, fixed-term nature of appointments implies expectation of rapid impact; applicants should be prepared to prioritize and execute quickly rather than pursue long-term incremental projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural fit and benefits of serving
rubrics_metrics.description: “Fueled by a sense of service and relentless intellectual drive, DARPA PMs enjoy unparalleled freedom... PMs immerse themselves in the DARPA culture and team, collaborating with luminaries across broad technical disciplines.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should appreciate DARPA’s high-autonomy, high-expectation culture. The page also lists benefits (competitive compensation, relocation support, LEED-certified office, alumni network) as rationale for joining.
